en: The Fisher Stair: The Last of the Low Town
A wet, plated thing the size of a hound that climbs sheer stone as easily as sand. It goes for the hand-line, not the hands, as if it knows the rope is what keeps people alive.
A gull-shaped hole in the rain, edged with a cold cyan shimmer. It dives at anything that moves fast, and nothing on the wall moves faster than a hauled rope.
A spawn-polyp rooted in the carved faces of the Watchers' stones. It cannot move, so it mends whatever climbs past it. Burning it off scars the carving underneath.
Not a creature. A limb of the storm itself, a column of black water and cloud that closes on the wall-head like a hand. Its wounds bleed cyan, and they do not matter to it.
Each turn of the Fisher Stair brings climbers up. A crawler's grip pushes it back: Toma's Hold the Stair takes the grip instead.
Liss can haul the stair to speed the climb, but the Squall Wings dive a hauled rope.
The Kirru draws one moving spawn off with each Storm-Call. The rooted polyp mends the crawlers: only the party can bring it down.
The storm's hand is closing on the stair. Use Toma's Hold the Stair before it lands to take the blow.
The dark blinds the party and slows the climbers. Call Virel: his full gauge unleashes Flare Line, which lights the stair.
Nothing can touch it. Get the last of them up.
The last of them are up.
Toma holds the stair. He will not leave it to strike.
A gull harrier gone dark with the weather. It rides the updraught off the headland without a wingbeat, and the static it carries crackles in its feathers before it spits it.
A reef crab the colour of laterite, grown fat on the seawall's weed. Corrow's children say it is a piece of the wall that got bored and walked off.
Not spawn. A soot-moth as wide as a door, drawn up Coilspire's flues by the keeping flame. It drinks fire and sheds soot, and the Tenders sweep its dust off the braziers every morning.
Go up the mole steps onto the seawall, among the Watchers.
The trial is at Coilspire, out on the headland. Go through the wall-gate.
The Fisher Stair runs down from the wall into the low town.
Follow the headland path up to the spire door.
A keeper tends a low fire in the hut at the spire's foot.
Turn the flue-keys. Let the flame climb the spire, tier by tier.
The flame has reached the crown. Climb up to it.
Turn the great key and light the beacon. The coast has to know.
